rep.angle: lead with a peer company's result
rep.name: Rohan

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hey, Marcus here. You've got about twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Thanks, Marcus. A peer fintech cut AE ramp by two months with HyperSale’s AI roleplays and quote-backed scoring—are reps practicing consistently today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Not consistently. Managers do some roleplaying during onboarding, but after that it’s pretty ad hoc.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Right, HyperSale gives every AE realistic buyer practice and managers quote-backed weekly scoring. Is your seven-month ramp mainly hurting pipeline coverage?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Not mainly. The product is technical, and newer reps fumble integration questions on live calls; that’s what tends to drag out the first deal.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: HyperSale’s weekly dashboards show who’s improving, and every score links to exact rep language. Would your VP of Sales want that visibility?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Possibly—Rachel owns this, not me. But how does that actually work for technical integration questions: do we build the scenarios and scoring rubric, or do you learn them from our calls and product materials?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: We’d configure scenarios from your product materials and manager input, then align the rubric together. Could Rachel join a follow-up demo?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Maybe. Before I pull Rachel in, how is this different from roleplaying with a manager beyond being available on demand, and what exactly would you show her?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Basically, the AI stays consistent and quote-backed, so managers track improvement without running every session. I’d show scenarios, scoring, and the dashboard—should we reconnect?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Not yet. What happens to the roleplay recordings and transcripts—are they used to train your models, where are they stored, and what retention and access controls do we get?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: I don’t want to misstate our security terms. We can cover training, storage, retention, and access controls with our security lead—would that help?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: It would, but send the security documentation first—I don’t want just verbal assurances. Then propose a specific time and agenda covering the technical scenario, scoring setup, and those four security points.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: I’ll send the security documentation today. How about Tuesday at 2 ET to cover scenarios, scoring, model training, storage, retention, and access controls?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Tuesday at 2 Eastern works, assuming I get the security documentation beforehand. Send the invite with that agenda; I’ll add Rachel, and please bring your security lead. Okay, I need to jump to standup.
